title: India's crude steel output just hit a new high for September - and demand is growing even faster. November 3, 2026.
excerpt: From an economist who measured progress by what people could actually do, to a Canadian immigrant award for an India-born actor-writer-producer, to a steel output record outpaced by even faster demand, to a homemaker turned 25-tonne-a-year fish farmer - November 3's four stories are about measuring the right thing, not just the biggest number.
bodyHtml:
Every story today is about a measure that matters more than the obvious one - capability instead of GDP, creative ownership instead of just a role, demand outpacing supply instead of supply alone, and one woman's income instead of an industry average.

He measured a country's progress by what its people could actually do - not just its GDP

Amartya Sen, born November 3, 1933, in Santiniketan, Bengal, became the first Asian to win the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in 1998. His 'capability approach' - development measured by what people can actually be and do, not just income - now underpins the Human Development Index.

She came to Canada from India at age four. In 2026, she was named one of its Top 25 immigrants

Supinder Wraich was named a Top 25 Canadian Immigrant Award winner for 2026 in the Arts & Culture category. Born in India, she created, wrote and starred in CBC Gem's 'The 410,' and won a 2025 Canadian Screen Award for her role in 'Allegiance.'

India's crude steel output just hit a new high for September - and demand is growing even faster

India's crude steel output rose 3.4% year-on-year to 14.1 million tonnes in September 2026. For H1 FY27, output reached 85.1 million tonnes while finished steel consumption grew even faster, up 7.5% - meaning India remained a net importer of finished steel even as production climbed.

She was a homemaker in Odisha who noticed fish farming on a reservoir - and decided to learn the trade herself

Sujata Bhuyan, from Sambalpur district, trained in cage-culture fish farming at the Hirakud Reservoir starting in 2022. She now produces 25-30 metric tonnes of fish a year, supplying markets across four states. PM Modi cited her in Mann Ki Baat's 132nd episode on March 29, 2026.

Four stories, one pattern: a Nobel laureate who redefined what counts as progress, an actor who writes and produces her own stories, an industry where demand is outrunning its own record output, and a homemaker who became an entrepreneur one training course at a time.
